captions.detailed: This 3D model is a customizable adjustment wheel, featuring a flat, circular body with numerous semi-circular notches distributed evenly around its outer edge for grip. At the center of the wheel is an elevated cylindrical collar that houses a hexagonal cavity designed to hold a nut. The main body of the wheel is thin, while the central collar extends higher to provide sufficient depth for the hexagonal nut chamber.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric adjustment wheel with circular notches around its perimeter and a central hexagonal cavity to secure a nut. The script should include adjustable parameters for the wheel diameter, wheel depth, nut diameter, nut depth, wall thickness of the nut chamber, the number of notches, and the notch diameter.
captions.factory: The script uses a difference() operation to subtract the nut cavity and the edge notches from the main wheel assembly. The main assembly is a union() of two cylinders: one representing the thin wheel body and another representing the elevated central nut collar. The hexagonal cavity is created by a linear_extrude() of a hexagon() shape from the MCAD library. The circular notches are subtracted using a for-loop that rotates and translates small cylinders around the perimeter of the wheel.
